children: Economic understanding should be within everyone’s reach.
Economics shapes the choices around us. Yet access to the tools for understanding it is far from equal.

OpenEconomics is a social impact initiative built around a simple conviction: where you begin should not determine what you can learn. Our work connects open educational resources with people who can help them reach further.
Make room for the voices behind the work: a student’s first workshop, an educator’s perspective, a library opening a new door.

The conviction behind the Open Economics Project.
Economics is part of everyday life. It shapes the choices people make, the institutions they rely on and the possibilities they can imagine.
Understanding it should be within reach. We want a learner’s curiosity to matter more than their access to expensive resources, a particular school or a reliable connection.
Build the relationships that help people use it.
A resource is only useful when someone can find it, understand it and put it to work. Our approach brings the digital academy together with publications, libraries and educational partners.

Local knowledge matters. Ambassadors and partners can help identify what is needed, where a resource fits and how it should change. We want those perspectives to influence the work from the beginning.
Clear explanations, thoughtful examples and careful review help learners develop understanding. Feedback should improve both what we teach and how we teach it.
Be accountable for the claims we make.
Reach, use and outcomes are different measures. We will distinguish them, explain our assumptions and make room for what the evidence cannot yet tell us.
What we build next, we build together.

specialisms.name: Development economics
specialisms.desc: Why do living standards differ, and what changes them?
specialisms.question: Can a higher GDP miss improvements in well-being?
specialisms.answer: Yes. GDP tracks production, while well-being also depends on health, education, distribution and environmental quality.

specialisms.name: Behavioral economics
specialisms.desc: Explore the gap between tidy models and real decisions.
specialisms.question: Why might a default change participation?
specialisms.answer: People may stick with an existing option because of inertia, limited attention or the effort required to change it.

specialisms.name: Financial economics
specialisms.desc: Connect saving, uncertainty and the value of time.
specialisms.question: Does diversification remove every kind of risk?
specialisms.answer: No. Spreading holdings can reduce asset-specific risk, but broad market risks can still affect the portfolio.

specialisms.name: Industrial organization
specialisms.desc: Study strategy, market power and how industries work.
specialisms.question: Why do barriers to entry matter?
specialisms.answer: They can protect incumbent firms from competition, influencing prices, innovation and long-run profits.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.intro: A commitment to making economic learning easier to access.
sections: Using the website
The site includes semantic navigation, keyboard focus states, responsive layouts and labeled controls. Accessibility testing continues as content develops.
Learning materials
The production approach should provide readable formats, meaningful descriptions for graphs and suitable alternatives where needed.
Known limitations
We work to make charts and learning resources accessible, including for people using assistive technologies.
Help & feedback
A dedicated contact process will support requests for accessible formats and reports of barriers.

licensing.title: Content licensing
licensing.intro: Clear permissions for sharing, printing and adapting economics resources.
sections: Check the individual resource
Each resource has its own license and attribution requirements. Contact our team about reuse of materials without an explicit license.
Print & distribute
Library and classroom permissions should clarify permitted copying, distribution and any conditions.
Translate & adapt
Resource-specific guidance should explain adaptation rights, attribution and the process for sharing translated versions.
Third-party material
Third-party images, quotations and other content may have separate terms. Ask before using material where the permission is unclear.

methodology.title: How we measure impact
methodology.intro: Definitions, reporting periods and evidence behind the numbers.
sections: Funding received & deployed
Report confirmed cash separately from pledges and in-kind support. Identify currency, reporting period and program expenditure.
Estimated costs avoided
Use documented use and an explicit comparable-cost baseline. Do not assume every download replaces a purchase. Report the scope, assumptions and possible overlap.
Reach, use & outcomes
Separate audience exposure, verified resource use and evidence of learning or improved access. Avoid adding overlapping groups into a single headline total.
Evidence, limitations & corrections
Record sources, dates and definitions. Describe missing data, update estimates when evidence changes and retain a clear correction history.
